einzeiler: Overcoming trauma, burnout, and business failure to master your mindset.
kurzfassung: Serial entrepreneur Kyle Livingston shares his extraordinary life story, from being abandoned as an infant to losing everything twice in business. He explains how he overcame extreme scarcity mindsets, burnout, and panic attacks to take control of his life and help other business owners scale. The conversation offers practical lessons on managing fear, recognizing patterns, and building mental resilience.
stichpunkte: Left at a yard sale at twelve weeks old after multiple attempted abortions by his birth mother, Kyle was adopted by a hardworking family in a rough neighborhood.
At age fourteen, after starting a neighborhood lawn-mowing and car-washing business, he realized he made more money in a day than his father did working two jobs.
Reading How to Win Friends and Influence People at sixteen fundamentally shifted his paradigm on success and goal-setting.
Driven by a scarcity mindset rooted in childhood poverty, he worked relentlessly toward a ten-thousand-dollar monthly goal, eventually suffering a severe panic attack and collapse at age twenty-six.
He lost everything twice in three years when his construction and business partnerships failed in 2016 and 2018.
To manage fear before taking big risks, he writes down every worst-case scenario on a legal pad to prove that the outcomes are manageable.
He now runs an agency helping online business owners generating over 150k monthly revenue build operational infrastructure and make data-driven decisions.
He enforces a strict rule of only working with business owners who have experienced past failure so they can spot warning signs early.

beschreibung:
Scarcity whispers that there isn't enough. Ego insists you deserve more anyway. Abundance is the quiet third option nobody mentions.

Most of us were handed scarcity as a default setting. This episode sits with that tension: what scarcity actually protects us from, why ego is so loyal to it, and what shifts when abundance becomes a practiced choice instead of a lucky feeling.

It's less about having more and more about needing less from the wrong things.

Ask what your ego is really protecting when it demands "more"

Treat abundance as a discipline you build, not a mood you wait for

Trace your scarcity triggers back to their original source
